long_biography.plain_text:
Avangard-Agro turned Kirill Minovalov's business interests into a vertically integrated chain stretching from fields and grain handling to malt plants in Russia and Germany. Established to secure barley for malting, the group expanded its land base, crop range, processing and exports. Minovalov's systems-engineering background is visible in its emphasis on centralised information, satellite monitoring and operational measurement.

Finance supplied the earlier platform. Minovalov created a consulting firm as a university student, then founded Bank Avangard in 1994 using capital that was partly borrowed. The bank grew after Russia's 1998 financial crisis and remained a core holding while he added agriculture and malting. He remains president and board chairman of Bank Avangard and supervisory-board chairman of Avangard Malz.

Official and audited sources establish control of the bank and agricultural group and a leadership connection to Avangard Malz, but the dossier does not attempt to map every intermediate holding entity or subsidiary.
